top_categories.workout_context: GFNY Walnut Creek's technical rolling roads into a major summit finish forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 64 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Walnut Creek's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
At GFNY Walnut Creek, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
107ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
6,909ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
6,909ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At GFNY Walnut Creek, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Walnut Creek. Train it until it feels boring.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on technical rolling roads into a major summit finish. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
64 miles on technical rolling roads into a major summit finish burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Low-cadence force work for 6,909ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
Smooth pedaling at 64 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for GFNY Walnut Creek’s 64 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at GFNY Walnut Creek. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at GFNY Walnut Creek demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride technical rolling roads into a major summit finish at race-day cadence weekly. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Dial in tire pressure before race week — 5 PSI wrong costs you 15+ minutes over 64 miles.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 64 miles of technical rolling roads into a major summit finish in Walnut Creek, California, USA.
